sections.title: Sound of emme
paragraphs: The letter (emme) /ˈɛmme/ makes the sound /m/. You hear this in the word (mare) /ˈma.re/, which means sea. This letter has only one sound in standard Italian.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Close both lips gently together. Send the air out through your nose. Turn on your voice. You can feel your throat vibrate, and your lips buzz softly.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: The letter makes the sound /m/ in all positions. For instance, you hear it clearly in (mamma) /ˈmam.ma/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: This sound is identical to the sound in the English word moon. Italian speakers never drop or alter this sound. You do not need to fix anything.
